title: Rahul Gandhi Is Taking the Exam Scandal Fight to Kota. Here Is What Congress Is Demanding.
excerpt: A nationwide campaign against paper leaks and CBSE failures starts on June 17, with student conventions planned across four cities. The party wants NEET decentralised and the education minister gone.
body:
Rahul Gandhi will lead a student convention in Kota on June 17, the opening event of a nationwide campaign the Indian National Congress says will target "the growing crisis of paper leaks, examination irregularities, unemployment and the systematic betrayal of India's youth."

The announcement, made by Congress General Secretary K.C. Venugopal on Saturday, comes amid two overlapping education scandals that have consumed India's political landscape: the CBSE On-Screen Marking controversy and the cancellation of NEET-UG 2026 after its question paper was leaked.

## Kota First, Then Allahabad, Patna and Delhi

The Congress has picked its venues strategically. Kota, Rajasthan's coaching capital where hundreds of thousands of students prepare for competitive exams, will host Gandhi on June 17. Allahabad follows on July 10, Patna on July 11, and Delhi on July 14.

At each stop, the party plans to bring together students, job aspirants, coaching centre operators, educators and youth organisations. The outreach will combine physical rallies with campus visits, social media campaigns, live screenings and direct dialogues at universities and coaching centres. The NSUI and Youth Congress will lead the mobilisation.

"Having repeatedly raised these issues, Rahul Gandhi has made the defence of merit, fairness and the availability of equal opportunity to our youth a pressing matter of national importance," Venugopal said.

## Two Scandals, One Campaign

The CBSE On-Screen Marking fiasco has escalated steadily since May. The board outsourced the digitisation of millions of Class 12 answer sheets to Coempt Edu Teck, a Hyderabad-based company previously known as Globarena Technologies — the same firm linked to the 2019 Telangana intermediate results disaster, where evaluation errors led to over 3.8 lakh students failing and at least 21 suicides.

A Delhi student, Vedant Shrivastava, discovered that the Physics answer sheet uploaded under his roll number contained entirely different handwriting. CBSE acknowledged the error and sent him the correct sheet, but the incident triggered a flood of complaints. Congress alleges that two million Class 12 answer sheets were exposed online through a misconfigured AWS storage bucket — a claim CBSE has denied, saying the portal cited in social media posts was not the one used for actual evaluation.

Separately, the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak forced the cancellation of the medical entrance exam and its rescheduling to June 21. The CBI has arrested multiple individuals, including educators and coaching institute operators, allegedly linked to the leak.

A 17-year-old researcher, Sarthak Sidhant, appeared before a parliamentary standing committee to present his findings on security flaws in CBSE's OnMark portal. The committee's involvement signals that the controversy has moved well beyond social media outrage into formal institutional scrutiny.

## Congress's Demands

The party is pushing four specific measures: decentralisation of NEET so that no single exam controls the fate of millions, abolition of examination fees, stricter legal action against those involved in paper leak rackets, and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, speaking after the strategy meeting where the campaign was finalised, said the country faced "serious challenges such as inflation, unemployment, exam scams and social inequality."

Jairam Ramesh, Congress's communications chief, linked the exam controversy to the broader US-India trade negotiations: "We have learned that a trade deal agreement will be reached on June 22. Farmers in Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, and Himachal Pradesh will be significantly affected."

## Why NRIs Should Care

The CBSE and NEET scandals directly affect diaspora families. Thousands of NRI and OCI students sit for CBSE board exams every year, either through affiliated schools abroad or as private candidates. NEET scores determine admission to Indian medical colleges — a pathway that many diaspora families actively pursue. A compromised examination system undermines the one thing these families count on: that merit will be fairly assessed.

Parents of the incoming Class 12 batch have already begun demanding assurances from schools about the security of digital platforms linked to board examinations. As one parent told Careers360: "They should be focusing on studying, not worrying about whether the systems connected to their examinations are reliable. That should not be their burden."

The Congress campaign is unlikely to produce immediate policy changes. But it has reframed the education crisis as an opposition rallying point ahead of state elections — and for millions of Indian students at home and abroad, that scrutiny is overdue.
